## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet, and the starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds. The default recipe gives only 32 PPO updates of 4096 samples, which is probably far too few for an exact-build task. The likely bottlenecks are the number of updates and how hard the placement rule is to learn. A placement is right if it lands at layer L (the highest filled cell under its footprint) and every footprint cell at L is still missing. In the starting network, a small MLP has to learn that interaction mixed across all layers. Plan: (1) keep the starting network and change only the recipe, to get more, smaller updates; (2) a network that scores each placement once per layer z, with weights shared across layers, then combines the layers with logsumexp. Per layer, the rule becomes a simple AND of footprint-pooled features. (3) The same network with a recipe that reuses samples more instead of collecting more.

### Round 2
All three trials scored 0, both on dev and on training success, so round 1 gives no ranking. The recipe changes did not rescue the baseline. The per-layer net with a layer embedding also failed. My reading is that the task can be solved by a local rule. A placement is safe if every cell it fills is missing at the landing layer, nothing missing lies below it in its columns, the build above is empty, and something supports it. The hard part is choosing the right layer. The baseline would have to learn that choice by multiplying features. The r1c2 embedding only adds a bias, which cannot pick out a layer's channels. The fix is to slice the input per layer z into a stack of layers counted relative to z: zero padding, slicing and concatenation are allowed before the first learned layer. One weight-shared 1x1 net then sees exactly the columns that matter, and footprint pooling can compute the AND/OR of the conditions. This round tests that idea, a recipe with more samples, and a learned footprint window that would still work if the stated footprint orientation is wrong.

### Round 3
All six trials scored exactly 0 on both seeds, and none built a single training design exactly in the last 10% of training. That held across three very different networks (the baseline, a per-layer net and a relative-layer net) and across 1, 2 and 4 PPO epochs. Seed noise cannot explain this, and changing the recipe alone did not help. Every network so far scores each action from the conv features at its own anchor cell. That only works if the action index maps to the anchor cell the way the task describes. The note says this world may not behave as described. If the action indices are transposed, permuted or anchored differently, no local head can learn, which would explain uniform zeros. I test that with a fully learned flat action head, alone and added to the baseline head. The third trial bets that the world is as described and only needs more samples: a cheaper relative-layer net with 1 epoch and higher gamma.

### Round 4
All nine trials scored exactly 0 on dev, and their training success was also 0. That held for local footprint heads, per-layer heads, flat Linear heads (which can learn any mapping from actions to cells), cheap and expensive networks, and 1 to 4 epochs. Since the flat head failed too, a twist in the action indexing alone is unlikely to explain it. A permutation of observation channels is also unlikely, because the generic 1x1 stems would cope with it. The most likely common cause is that the policy collapses early. A random placement usually earns a negative reward because it fills cells outside the target. DONE, a single action that ends the episode, then looks better than the average placement, so PPO with lr 1e-3 and low entropy (0.005 in most trials) may lock into pressing DONE early. The greedy evaluation would then build nothing. With the last 3 trials, I am testing stability and exploration: lower lr, higher entropy and a longer horizon. I am also trying a network that sees the action mask.
